# Data Types, Comparison Operators and Functions

```{note}
This page is partly adapted from by [Brett and co-authors (2023)](https://odsti.github.io/cfd-textbook/intro_to_functions.html). See the [license](https://github.com/pxr687/Intro_Comp_Programming/blob/main/license.md) page for more information.
```

Let's quickly summarise what we have learned so far.

A raw number or piece of text typed in Python code is called a *literal*:
<!-- #endregion -->

```{python}
100
```

```{python}
"text"
```

We type in the literal, and Python shows us the *value*. The value is the computer representation of the literal.

We can store values as *variables*. This means we give the value a name. We can use that name to get the value out of our computers' memory:

```{python}
# This is a variable assignment statement. 
#`number_3` is the name of the variable, `3` is its value.
number_3 = 3
```

```{python}
# The cell above this one created this variable `number_3`. This cell shows the value of the variable.
number_3
```

You can think of literals as values in Python code which are NOT stored as variables:

```{python}
# This is a literal.
1999
```

```{python}
# Store `1999` as a variable.
new_variable = 1999
```

We have also talked about expressions - any piece of Python code that returns a value:

```{python}
# This is an expression.
2 + 2
```

```{python}
# This is also an expression, because it returns a value (it is the variable we made earlier)
number_3
```

```{python}
# This literal is also an expression, beause it returns a value.
1990
```

We have also use *functions*, like `print()`:

```{python}
# The `print()` function.
print('This is the print functon!')
```

You can think of a function like a [*recipe*](https://www.inferentialthinking.com/chapters/08/Functions_and_Tables). We give it some ingredients, and it returns a "meal".

For the `print()` function, we give it some input and it displays the input. We used it for text, but we can also use it for numbers:

```{python}
# The `print()` function (again).
print(10)
```

[Importance of type]

```{python}
# A number, multiplied by 10.
10 * 10
```

```{python}
# Text, multiplied by 10.
"This is text!" * 10
```

[TYPE IS VERY IMPORTANT, LOSING TRACK OF IT WILL CAUSE ERRORS!]

`type()` function can tell us...

```{python tags=c("raises-exception")}
type()
```

[Explain arguments, using `print()` again as example]

```{python}
type(1)
```

```{python}
type("Hello world!")
```

```{python}
# 
help(type)
```

```{python tags=c("raises-exception")}
help(type())
```

```{python}
# Assign a numeric variable.
my_number = 10
```

```{python}
# Show the value of `my_number`.
my_number
```

```{python}
type(my_number)
```

```{python}
# Assign another numeric variable.
my_other_number = 10.0
```

```{python}
# Show the value of `my_other_number`.
my_other_number
```

```{python}
type(my_other_number)
```

[List of basic datatypes]


## Why is Data Type important?

...because the wrong data type will break your code!

```{python}
10 * 10
```

```{python tags=c("raises-exception")}
"10" * "10"
```

## Comparison operators and Booleans

- Explain link to literals, variables, expressions and datatypes.

- Explain importance with concrete example.

```{python}
10 == 10
```

```{python}
type(10 == 10)
```

```{python}
type(True)
```

```{python}
type("True")
```

```{python}
True * 10
```

```{python}
"True" * 10
```

```{python}
10 == 11
```

```{python}
10 < 10
```

```{python}
10 < 11
```

```{python}
10 > 10
```

```{python}
10 > 9
```

```{python}
10 != 11
```

```{python}
10 != 10
```

```{python}
# Equality comparison operator, with variables.
my_number == my_other_number
```

```{python}
my_extra_number = 200

# Show the value of `my_extra_number`
my_extra_number
```

```{python}
my_number == my_extra_number
```

```{python}
is_true = my_number == my_other_number

is_true
```

```{python}
type(is_true)
```

```{python}
is_false = my_number == my_extra_number

is_false
```

```{python}
type(is_false)
```

```{python}
"This string is the same" == "This string is the same"
```

```{python}
"This string is the same" == "This string is NOT the same"
```

```{python}
type("This string is the same" == "This string is NOT the same")
```

## Changing Data Types

[Can be done with built-in functions]

```{python}
my_int = 10

my_int
```

```{python}
my_float = float(my_int)

my_float
```

```{python}
type(my_int)
```

```{python}
type(my_float)
```

```{python}
my_string = str(my_float)

my_string
```

```{python}
type(my_string)
```
